memory_candidates.content: When a verify-deploy.sh-style gate's per-file byte ceiling is tight (within ~1-2%), always re-measure sub-checks that share the SAME landed sibling commit as the one that unblocked a precondition -- a commit that satisfies one precondition (e.g. 'the file is no longer concurrently edited') can simultaneously grow that same file past an unrelated ceiling. Don't assume a Non-Goal file stays stable just because it's out of file_scope; re-check it live immediately before flipping any gate mode that covers it.

When trimming prose to hit a byte budget and a verification step greps for a literal substring (e.g. 'MUST NOT'), preserve that literal substring even when rewording for brevity -- a semantically-equivalent bolded rephrasing ('**Never emit...**') can silently drop a mechanical grep-count check that depends on the literal text, not the meaning.

A fixture-driven test suite that real-copies the live repo tree (rsync) as its 'clean baseline' will fail its baseline-cleanliness assertion whenever ANY other concurrently-running task has landed source-store edits not yet redeployed to .claude/, or has live uncommitted edits to shared files like specs/TODO.md/state.json -- this is cross-task staleness, not a regression from the task under test. Confirm via an isolated git worktree checkout of the pre-task commit before concluding a baseline-fixture test failure is a real regression.
